🔍 Gravitate-Health was built on a simple principle: 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗹𝘁𝗵 𝗶𝗻𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 should empower people and improve health outcomes. After almost 6 years, partners from across sectors have worked together to develop 𝗶𝗻𝗻𝗼𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲, 𝗽𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝘀𝗼𝗹𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗱𝗶𝗴𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗹𝘁𝗵 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗲𝗱, 𝗲𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗱, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗲𝗺𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀. The project's achievements demonstrate that scientific excellence and real-world applicability must go hand in hand to create lasting impact. The consortium showcased the 𝘃𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝗰-𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽𝘀 and 𝗺𝘂𝗹𝘁𝗶-𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗵𝗼𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗰𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗯𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, bringing together patients, healthcare professionals, regulators, researchers, industry and technology experts. As Europe moves toward the implementation of the European Health Data Space (EHDS) and the upcoming widespread adoption of ePI, 𝗚𝗿𝗮𝘃𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗲-𝗛𝗲𝗮𝗹𝘁𝗵 𝗵𝗮𝘀 𝗽𝗮𝘃𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗮𝘆 for a future where individuals can access, understand, and manage their health information effectively. Among the consortium's key achievements are: 🔹 FHIR ePI Implementation Guide 🔹 Gravitate-Health Open Source Technology Platform 🔹 Gravitate-Health Collaborative Community These innovations contribute to a more connected, interoperable, and patient-centered healthcare ecosystem. Besides the achievements, we would like to also celebrate the 𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗴 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆 built along the way. Thank you to all consortium partners, contributors, and stakeholders for their collaboration throughout this remarkable journey💙 Innovative Health Initiative (IHI) EFPIA - European Federation of Pharmaceutical Industries and Associations ...more ...more

What if the boundaries between biology and technology ceased to exist? Today, the fusion of biological systems and advanced technology is no longer theoretical – it’s happening. From brain-computer interfaces to drug simulations that replicate human organs on a chip, we are pushing beyond the limitations of hardware and software, offering a bold way forward in medicine and beyond. Curious about how this fusion of biology and technology could shape the future of medicine and beyond? Then read on as I explore how biology's adaptability can drive innovation in healthcare, sharing examples of advances already underway and the ethical and technical challenges they present. I’d be keen to hear your thoughts in the comments – where do you see the greatest promise? And what questions do you think we need to be asking next? #Innovation #Wetware ...more ...more

Join us at the DIA Medical Information and Communications Conference this September! This is where forward-thinking professionals come together to explore what’s next in medical information. Here’s what you will gain: ◾ Insights into the impact of evolving business, regulatory, and legal requirements on daily medical information practices. ◾ An understanding of how advancements in digital technologies and AI are transforming information delivery and customer engagement. ◾ A look out at the role of automation, digital innovation, and real-world evidence in enhancing customer communications — while remaining compliant with all relevant guidelines. ◾ Practical approaches to showcasing the strategic value of medical information within your organisation. The call for posters is still open. Share your work, showcase your expertise, and contribute to the conversation. An electronic survey containing 71 closed and open-ended questions was distributed to 36 phactMI member companies. The survey included questions on demographics, the development of specific content such as scientific response documents (SRDs) and custom response documents, and metrics and KPIs. This benchmarking survey assessed the evolving approach and tactics of content development and utilization of KPIs of phactMI member companies with a comparison to our 2018 survey, where applicable. The results are now published. Let us know what stands out to you: https://lnkd.in/gNFUxFXQ 📝 : Robert Tamburri , Mary Sendi, Anja Glaetzer MD, PhD, PGDip Health Economics , Jennifer G. , Mary M. , Susan Wnorowski PharmD, BCMAS, Evelyn Hermes DeSantis #medicalinformation #futuremi #ai #srd #medicalaffairs

Next week I'm giving a keynote at the MILE - Medical Information Leaders in Europe Summer Member Meeting 2026 in Surrey, UK. 🇬🇧 My talk is called "The Unsanctioned Advisor." I'll be sharing some of CAIRO, Inc. 's cross-therapy-area research on how today's leading AI models represent medicines, and how this new, unmonitored channel is now feeding directly into patient, payor and physician decisions. How to govern this new technology will be a vital question for medical information leaders in the coming years. A sincere thank-you to Michelle Bridenbaker , Helen Surrey , Stefne Pienaar , Julie Hayden and the whole MILE committee for the invitation. It's a real privilege to speak in front of an audience like this one.
